description: Canonical frozen v2 baseline — single source of truth for the ablation spine. Regression-guarded by tests/test_baseline_v2_manifest.py, which re-aggregates each cell's stored per-query jsonl and asserts it matches these numbers. This guards the aggregation/metric code during v3 Phase A refactoring. It does NOT re-run the pipeline (that needs Docker + Ollama + a full re-eval); a full re-run against this manifest is the separate spine re-validation done once after Phase A.

metric.note: recall_at_k_strict is SQuAD-comparable (headline); recall_at_k_fuzzy is lenient. Aggregation = mean of non-None per-question recall over QASPER dev questions with non-empty gold evidence.

decisions.config_B_setting: section router t0.3 n1 (honest: ~neutral vs flat). Oracle routing recorded separately as headroom, not as an ablation cell.
decisions.config_E_status: retrieval MEASURED = 0.692 fuzzy (WORSE than C/D ~0.77 — citation expansion dilutes in-paper recall@5); verification DEFERRED (CUDA-bound, documented in eval/results/README.md)

A_flat_baseline.description: Flat chunking (BGE), no routing, no expansion — pure baseline

B_section_router.description: A + section-aware chunking + query router (t0.3, top_n=1) — ~neutral vs flat at best setting

B_embed_router.description: R1b improvement cell: B config (t0.3, top_n=1) with the BGE-embedding router (EmbeddingRouter) replacing TF-IDF. Neutral vs flat (0.739): discriminates better than TF-IDF (dev macro-F1 0.376 vs 0.306) but 'other' still wins top-1 for 990/1002 questions, so the other-fallback reverts to flat. New cell alongside frozen B_section_router; frozen cells untouched.

B_embed_router_no_other.description: R1b.1 DIAGNOSTIC (not a shippable config): embedding router with --router-exclude-other, testing the crude 'never predict other' hack instead of the flat fallback. Recall CRASHES to 0.609 (< flat 0.738), matching TF-IDF's ~0.60 from R1a. This rules out the exclude-other hack, not routing in general: the oracle section set includes 'other' for 45.2% of questions and is 'other'-only for 15.1%, so blanket-excluding 'other' discards evidence that legitimately lives in 'other'-tagged chunks. What R1b established: a LINEAR head (TF-IDF or BGE-embedding) collapses to predicting 'other' top-1 for ~99% of questions — it cannot tell WHEN evidence is section-specific. The oracle (0.866) proves that selective distinction exists in the data; whether a stronger/fine-tuned classifier (R1c) can learn it is UNTESTED. Conclusion: the two cheap configs (fallback→flat, exclude-other→0.609) both fail; realizing headroom needs a selective router, which the linear heads do not provide.

B_embed_router_union.description: R1b.2 IMPROVEMENT: embedding router at the frozen B config (t0.3, top_n=1) but with 'other' treated as a searchable section (--no-router-other-fallback) instead of triggering the flat fallback. Same threshold as frozen B — only the fallback semantics change (flat -> union of predicted labels including 'other'). Result 0.7448 fuzzy / 0.2059 strict: the FIRST section-router config to beat flat A (0.7380 / 0.2016) on both metrics. Mechanism: light filtering drops the lowest-confidence section while keeping 'other', cutting a bit of top-5 dilution without losing the 'other'-bucket evidence. Gain is small (+0.68pt fuzzy over A) because at t0.3 the predicted set is still ~6 sections; higher thresholds filter harder but CRASH (t0.5 -> 0.556) since the linear head can't accurately pick small sets. Realizing the 0.866 oracle headroom is gated on classifier accuracy (R1c fine-tune, untested), but union is the correct routing semantics to pair it with.

B_distilbert_router_union.description: R1c NEGATIVE (CPU budget): fine-tuned DistilBERT router (66M, 6 epochs CPU, sqrt-capped balanced BCE, lr warmup) with union routing at the frozen B config (t0.3/n1). Result 0.6360 fuzzy / 0.1653 strict — BELOW flat A (0.7380) and well below the embedding-union ceiling (0.7448). Two failure modes bracket it: unweighted BCE collapses rare classes to zero; full neg/pos balancing forces predict-all (recovers flat by NOT filtering, ~0.739). The fair middle (this cell) is genuinely discriminative (healthy per-class P/R, macro-F1 0.343) yet routes WRONG when it commits — confident section picks that exclude evidence-bearing chunks. Threshold sweep confirms it asymptotes to flat as threshold->0 (t0.15 -> 0.727) and never exceeds it. Lesson: discrimination != routing accuracy; realizing the 0.866 oracle headroom needs accuracy no CPU-trainable model (linear head OR DistilBERT) achieves. Proper R1c would need GPU-scale training and may still fail (question-text->section is a weak signal). NOTE: distilbert eval requires OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 (faiss/torch OpenMP clash segfaults otherwise). Union (0.7448) remains the local best.

B_oracle_ceiling.description: Reference ceiling (oracle section routing) — routing headroom, NOT an ablation cell

C_rerank_mxbai.description: R2 NEGATIVE (reranker swap): same config as frozen C (flat + cross-encoder rerank, retrieve_k=10) but with mixedbread-ai/mxbai-rerank-base-v1 instead of ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2. Result 0.7600 fuzzy / 0.2211 strict — BELOW frozen C's L-6 (0.7712 / 0.2205) on the headline fuzzy metric (ties on strict, within noise). mxbai was the best of three tested alternatives; all lose to L-6 on fuzzy: L-12 sibling 0.7593, bge-reranker-base (multilingual) 0.7234 (below flat A 0.7380). Conclusion: MiniLM-L-6 is already the sweet spot for this scientific-QA rerank at retrieve_k=10 — bigger (L-12), different-family (bge), and modern-English (mxbai) rerankers all underperform it. Reranker choice is NOT a lever. NOTE: frozen C's description says 'B + citation expansion' but its actual run config was flat+rerank (no router/expansion per its summary) — pre-existing description drift, frozen cell left untouched.

C_rerank_depth_k30.description: R3 NEGATIVE (candidate depth): frozen C config (flat + L-6 rerank) but with retrieve_k=30 instead of 10 — a wider funnel for the reranker to rescue chunks the bi-encoder underranked. Result 0.7685 fuzzy / 0.2159 strict — BELOW frozen C's retrieve_k=10 (0.7712 / 0.2205). Sweep {20,30,50} all land ~0.767-0.769 (saturated): widening the pool slightly HURTS, because deeper candidates add distractors the reranker occasionally promotes over true evidence. k=10 is already optimal. With R2 (reranker model, also negative), both halves of the rerank pipeline are saturated — the C ceiling (~0.771) is not movable by local rerank tuning.

D_multihop.description: B + multi-hop reasoning (LangGraph decomposition) over reranked retrieval

E_full_system.description: Full-system retrieval: B + citation expansion (C) + multi-hop (D), stacked
E_full_system.note: FINDING: stacking is WORSE than either component alone (C=0.771, D=0.772 fuzzy). Citation expansion is the culprit — on QASPER gold evidence is in-paper, so 1-hop neighbor chunks dilute precision@5 (cf. week6_rerank_k10_expand=0.691, near-identical). Multihop adds nothing (mean sub-qs 1.05). Honest ablation result: more components != better; expansion helps cross-paper F1 (its intended purpose) but hurts in-paper recall@5, so the 'full system' should NOT enable expansion for QASPER-style retrieval. Verification leg = scifact_finetuned below.

scifact_zeroshot.description: Zero-shot DeBERTa NLI (MoritzLaurer/DeBERTa-v3-base-mnli-fever-anli) on SciFact abstract-level labels

scifact_finetuned.description: Fine-tuned DeBERTa NLI on SciFact — the verification lift over zero-shot
scifact_finetuned.note: Not a missing to-do: deliberately deferred, documented in eval/results/README.md (week9_scifact_finetune). DeBERTa-v2 disentangled attention NaNs on Apple Silicon MPS within ~20 steps; CPU fine-tune ~60h (~4 min/step). Scaffolding shipped + tested (scripts/train_nli.py, tests/test_train_nli.py); runs on CUDA with no code change. Shipped verification number remains zero-shot 0.691.
